catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class fits the controller reset. cap.motion.home.v1 is a homing move to a declared home position or reference switch; the upstream reset only sends the axis-specific '<axis>OR;<axis>WS0' line (esp.py:22-23), and the clone never defines a home position or a reference switch. cap.motion.stop.v1 is a safe stop, which the reset is not documented to be. The extension action has no input and reports whether the controller returned no error (TE?) after the reset.

notes:
PASSED ON THE FAKE BACKEND ONLY by python3 -m mhs.driver check MHS/drivers/labs/hrosiak__esp301 --backend fake; all gates G1-G9 passed and the report contains no warning. Evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. gate.digest is the digest the gate printed for the passing report; check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package. Model-authored and unreviewed: driver.lock.json authored_by is the model, reviewed_by is null; hardware was never attached, the hardware backend was never started, and nothing here ran on a controller or a stage.

DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: the card proposes a SerialDriver (family serial, decision family-config, helper SerialDriver), but the upstream assembles every line from an axis number and a command letter at run time: reset writes '<axis>OR;<axis>WS0' (esp.py:22-23) and setpos writes '<axis>PA<pos>;<axis>WS1;<axis>TP' (esp.py:36-42). A fixed command table cannot reproduce those lines, so this package is a direct Driver over esp:esp with a native.py hardware factory; a maintainer can correct the card with an override.

Scope and coverage: reads are the served axis position (getpos, TP), returned in the controller's own position units, and the controller error number (check_errors, TE?). The one write is target_position: setpos (PA) on the served axis, with Limit.operator_required because the clone states no travel range and only accepts the float the caller gives (esp.py:36-42). The action x-cap.hrosiak.reset_axis.v1 sends the upstream reset and refuses with MHS.DEVICE.FAULTED if TE? returns a nonzero error. The served axis is the upstream defaxis, so the hardware factory requires dev, baudrate and axis; the fake's axis 1 and all other fake numbers are '# placeholder' test data, not facts. The clone has no tests, simulator or recording (task.mock_strategy.upstream_tests is null and hints are empty), so the card's preferred transcript was not available and the package uses an in-memory fake whose public methods are exactly reset, check_errors, getpos and setpos.

NOT COVERED: the composite upstream position(pos) helper (it calls setpos, getpos and setpos again; esp.py:44-49), and the raw serial transport, baud-rate selection, axis lists beyond the one served axis, velocity/acceleration/limit-switch configuration (the clone exposes no such methods). There is no transcript because the clone contains no recorded session.

Limits and safety: site-limits.example.json uses 0.0 and 20.0 only because those are the clone's initpos constructor default (esp.py:4) and README usage position (README.md:13); it is an example overlay that makes the conformance run able to write, not a statement about any stage, and the real bench must supply its own minimum and maximum. Without an operator overlay every position write is refused MHS.SAFETY.LIMITS_UNSET. The clone defines no stop, abort or halt method (esp.py:22-49): the e-stop and the reset action send the upstream reset ('<axis>OR;<axis>WS0'), and this package does not claim that the reset stops a move already in progress. The device is motion.axis at R1; no independent hardware stop is declared or tested, and none was invented.
